core_obligations: Reduce all three parts to one observation (proof lines 12695-12696): for every etale morphism U -> X with U nonempty, the generic point eta of the irreducible scheme X lies in the image of U -> X.

Use the observation to force the inclusion of the subsheaf to be an equality on sections (statement lines 12678-12690 with the proof): since every nonempty etale open carries a point over eta, a section of the ambient constant sheaf that lies in G at the generic point lies in G everywhere, so G agrees with the constant sheaf determined by its generic-point value.

Read off the three parts: for sets (part 1), abelian groups (part 2) and modules over Lambda (part 3), the subsheaf G squeezed between underline S' and underline S (respectively A'/A, M'/M) is determined by the value at the generic point, hence equals underline S' (respectively underline A', underline M').
proof_roadmap: Note that every nonempty etale open U of an irreducible scheme X maps onto a set containing the generic point eta.
Hence a section that lies in the subsheaf at the generic point lies in it on every nonempty etale open.
Apply this to the three settings, sets, abelian groups and modules.
Conclude G equals the corresponding constant subsheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma has three parts, for sets, abelian groups and modules over a ring, all of the same shape: a subsheaf of the constant sheaf underline S that contains underline S' and whose stalk at the generic point is S' must be underline S' itself (statement lines 12674-12692). The whole content is compressed into one observation, that for every etale morphism U -> X with U nonempty the generic point eta of the irreducible X lies in the image of U (proof lines 12695-12696); from it, agreement at the generic point propagates to every nonempty etale open. The claim is H2: the statement is long because it is stated in three parallel settings, while the proof is a single geometric observation applied three times.
